title: Virat Kohli Locked in as Automatic Pick for 2027 World Cup as Selectors Move Past Rohit Sharma
excerpt: Head coach Gautam Gambhir and chief selector Ajit Agarkar are aligned on Kohli's place in India's ODI plans, while Rohit has been told he is no longer in the selectors' scheme of things after the England tour.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Virat Kohli confirmed as automatic pick for the 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa
  • Rohit Sharma informed by selectors he is no longer in their plans beyond the England series
  • Kohli has scored 961 runs in 18 ODIs since 2025, averaging over 60

India head coach Gautam Gambhir and chief selector Ajit Agarkar have agreed that Virat Kohli will be an automatic pick for the 2027 ODI World Cup, which will be co-hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia. The decision comes as the team management simultaneously informed Rohit Sharma that he is no longer in their scheme of things for ODIs beyond the ongoing England tour.

Kohli's Form Speaks for Itself

The former Indian captain has been in commanding form in the one format he remains active in. Since the start of 2025, Kohli has scored 961 runs in 18 ODIs, averaging over 60 — making him India's second-highest run-getter in the format during that period.

While he scored just 5 in the first ODI against England at Edgbaston, Kohli returned to form with a 65-run knock off 66 deliveries in the second match at Cardiff, becoming India's leading run-scorer across all formats in England, overtaking Rahul Dravid.

The team management has no issues with his form or fitness, according to news agency PTI. Kohli missed the previous series against Afghanistan due to injury but received clearance from the BCCI just before the England series.

End of the Road for Rohit?

The contrast with Rohit Sharma's situation is stark. A BCCI source told PTI: "Selectors have informed Rohit he is not in their scheme of things post the England tour and they are moving on from him after this series. Though he wanted to continue, especially after working on his fitness. The selectors have left the ball in Sharma's court to decide his future."

Rohit, 39, registered scores of 16, 48, and 79 in the recent Afghanistan series, showing he could still perform. But the age factor and the management's desire to blood younger players have tipped the balance. Yashasvi Jaiswal is seen as the likely replacement at the top of the order.

Rotation Policy in Play

India's team management is also pushing a rotation policy for senior players ahead of the 2027 World Cup. The goal is to avoid a situation where a senior player breaks down mid-series with no tested replacement ready.

"The team management doesn't want a situation where a senior player breaks down and there is no one ready with enough game time," sources said. The policy would also involve managing KL Rahul's workload, with Ishan Kishan being developed as a backup wicketkeeper.

A Generational Shift

The development marks a significant moment in Indian cricket's transition. While Kohli continues to deliver, the selectors are clearly building a younger core around captain Shubman Gill. The England ODI series — with its final match at Lord's on July 19 — could be Rohit Sharma's last in India colors, ending an era that saw him score 33 ODI centuries and lead the team to the 2023 World Cup final.

For millions of diaspora cricket fans, the series finale at Lord's carries the weight of a farewell — and the promise of what comes next under Gill and Kohli's continued presence.
